conviction_note: The quarter being reported was pre-announced on 2026-09-03 as at or above the top of the guide, so the print turns on the first Q4 guide (consensus about $334m revenue, $0.39 EPS) and on how carriers spend in Q4. The evidence for that guide points both ways: Progressive's Q3 policy adds slowed sharply, but its 88.7 combined ratio leaves room to keep spending, and peers called carrier demand healthy in August. abs_move is held near the name's 14.2% median reaction, trimmed only because Q3 is pre-released; p_up sits at 49, a coin flip. The sum of the findings (-0.60) and the scaled number (-0.24) are both near zero and agree in sign.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue at or above $355.0m, contribution $54.5m and adj. EBITDA $35.0m, the top of the 2026-07-29 guide, which the company said on 2026-09-03 it would meet or beat (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818383/000181838326000229/exhibit991pressrelease.htm). Sell-side Q3 revenue estimates disagree: $353.8m with EPS $0.36 (Benzinga, seen as a search snippet only) and a stale $341.7m (https://www.earningswhispers.com/epsdetails/MAX). Q4 consensus is about $334m revenue (Benzinga, snippet) and $0.39 EPS from 3 analysts (https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/523427-what-you-need-to-know-about-mediaalpha-incs-q3-earnings, dated 2026-10-28; that page mislabels Q2 figures as Q3). The Q3 bar rests on the company's own guide. The Q4 bar comes from estimate sources only, so findings on the guide are kept small.
positioning_check: Short interest is 3,219,791 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, 5.3% of 61.26m shares outstanding, with 2.78 days to cover (it was 2,831,462 on 09-30). Source: https://equibles.com/stocks/max/short-interest?range=3m. Not crowded. Baseline 25-delta skew is -10.16 vol points (calls bid over puts, 'upside paid'), put/call open interest 0.41, front-expiry ATM IV 76.9%. The ATM spread is 96% of mid, so the chain is barely usable and the skew is a weak statement. The 20-day run-up is +22.57%. The sector moved together: from 2026-09-23 to 10-22 MAX went 9.39 to 12.41, EverQuote 17.63 to 23.59 and QuinStreet 14.28 to 16.88 (Yahoo chart v8). Positioning leans long into the print.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-03 MediaAlpha told the market Q3 revenue, contribution and adj. EBITDA would be at or above the top of the guide ($355.0m / $54.5m / $35.0m). The Benzinga Q3 revenue consensus of $353.8m still sits just below that floor. In Q2 revenue beat the top of the guide by 2.2% ($316.9m vs $310m), so a print of about $360-365m is plausible: a beat against consensus that the company already flagged.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q2 2026 revenue beat the top of the guide ($316.9m vs $290-310m) and EPS was $0.65 vs about $0.21 consensus, yet the stock fell 1.88% (baseline 2026-07-29). In Q1 2026, a record quarter (revenue +17%), it fell 14.9%. This name does not pay for reported-quarter beats.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The update is public, and the stock fell from about $12.2 (2026-09-02, per director Form 144 sale prices) to $9.2 by 09-28 despite it. The only unpriced part is the gap between the lagging consensus ($353.8m) and the company's own floor, plus any beat above the top end. If the market had fully priced a $360m+ quarter, consensus would sit above $355m. It does not.
findings.independence: Q2 2026 investor supplement, a different document from the same issuer: Q2 cleared the top of its guide by $6.9m (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001818383/000181838326000198/maxq22026-investorsuppleme.htm).

findings.finding: Progressive, very likely one of MediaAlpha's three customers above 10% of revenue (together 57% of Q2 revenue per the 10-Q), is adding auto policies much more slowly. Direct auto policies in force rose 127k in Q3 2026 (16,721k at 06-30 to 16,848k at 09-30) against 374k in Q3 2025 (15,245k to 15,619k). Agency auto rose 136k against 207k a year earlier. Total policies in force were flat from August to September (40,492k to 40,489k), and Personal Lines net premiums written grew 1% in September. Profitability is still strong: Q3 combined ratio 88.7 vs 89.5.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q4 guide decides the reaction. Q4 2025's guide of $280-300m came in 1.3% below consensus (tipranks/thefly), yet the stock rose 15.4% on 2026-02-23 on buyback and earnings. Q2 2026's Q3 guide of $330-355m sat above a ~$338m consensus and the stock still fell 1.9%. The record on this line is mixed.
findings.why_not_priced: Progressive released this on 2026-10-14, after MediaAlpha last spoke on 09-03, and nobody has turned policy counts into a MediaAlpha Q4 number. MAX rose 9.8% on 10-15, the day after, which is not what the price would do if the market read it as a pullback signal. If it were priced, MAX would have lagged its peers in October. It ran with them. Caveat: slower policy growth does not mean lower ad spend. Progressive's Q2 10-Q (search snippet, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000080661/000008066126000308/pgr-20260630.htm) shows advertising up 16% with new applications up only 1%, so spend can stay high while it converts less. Progressive says it spends while it stays efficient and meets its profit target, and an 88.7 combined ratio leaves room for that. The size here is net of that counterweight.
findings.independence: Proxy: this is a counterparty number, not MediaAlpha's own. The customer-concentration figures come from MediaAlpha's own 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818383/000181838326000200/max-20260630.htm). June policy counts confirmed via https://collisionweek.com/2026/07/16/progressive-reports-personal-auto-policies-force-8-8-june-compared-2025/. Net of the rest: the other two large customers and the long tail would need to keep growing their budgets, and EverQuote's August commentary (finding below) says carriers broadly were.

findings.finding: The 20-day run-up of +22.6% is a sector rebound, not MediaAlpha-specific news. On 2026-09-22/23 EverQuote fell 14.6% and 9.8%, QuinStreet 11.5% and 6.5%, and MAX 7.5% and 5.9%; Tickeron tied the selloff to analyst actions, insider sales and risk-off, not a carrier event. Since 09-23 MAX is up 25% to its 10-22 peak, EverQuote 34% and QuinStreet 18%. EverQuote (2026-11-02) and QuinStreet (2026-11-04) report after this window, so MAX is the first read on Q3 carrier spend in the group, and the stock goes in with options leaning long.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Baseline: of 7 prints, 4 rose and 3 fell, median absolute move 14.2%. After the July print, which followed a rally into it, the stock fell 1.9% on a beat-and-raise.
findings.why_not_priced: The run-up itself is in the price. What is not obvious is that it is peer beta rather than company news: no MediaAlpha filing or analyst action in October explains it. If the rally carried MAX-specific information, MAX would have outrun EverQuote, and it did not. The skew (-10 vol points, calls bid) points the other way. This finding is kept small because the chain is too wide (96% spread) to be a strong counter-signal.
findings.independence: Daily closes from Yahoo chart v8 for MAX, EVER and QNST (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/EVER?range=2mo&interval=1d). Peer report dates: https://finviz.com/news/401749/everquote-to-announce-third-quarter-2026-financial-results-on-november-2-2026 and https://finviz.com/news/402057/quinstreet-sets-date-to-announce-fiscal-first-quarter-2027-financial-results.

findings.finding: Peers described broad and growing carrier demand after MediaAlpha's last full print. EverQuote's Q2 2026 release (2026-08-03): revenue +25%, auto +23%, a major carrier back on the marketplace, carriers 'profitable and hungry for growth', and a Q3 guide of $198-208m. QuinStreet guided its September quarter to $370-380m against about $355m consensus, after auto insurance grew 37% the quarter before.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no clean record of MAX reacting to peer prints. Peer read-through is in the price by the time MAX reports.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it is August information, before MediaAlpha's own 09-03 update. It is filed because it is the broadest public evidence that carrier spend is broadening beyond Progressive, which bears on the Q4 guide. If the market doubted it, MAX would trade at a bigger discount to peers after the September selloff, and it does not.
findings.independence: QuinStreet fiscal Q4 2026 call, a separate company: https://www.benzinga.com/node/62315122 (QuinStreet's own results release not fetched).

findings.finding: Consumer shopping for auto insurance is slowing. The LexisNexis Insurance Demand Meter for Q2 2026 put year-over-year shopping growth at 1.4%, down from 3.2% in Q1 and 6.4% in Q3 2025. New-policy growth was 3.3%, and 36% of rate changes were decreases, a sign of a softening market.
findings.why_not_priced: It is an industry series, public since August, and MediaAlpha's own September statement that Q3 would land at or above the top end came after it, so for Q3 it is superseded. For Q4 it still matters: in a softening market carriers bid more per shopper for fewer shoppers, which helps price and hurts volume. Sign uncertain, so sized small.
findings.independence: Proxy. It shares the softening-market point with the Progressive finding but uses different data (industry shopping counts vs one carrier's policy counts).

findings.finding: On 2026-09-09 MediaAlpha bought out PLX's share of the tax receivable agreement (TRA) for $12.0m cash against a $22.7m liability, 47% below its estimated value. That should book a gain of about $10.7m below operating income in Q3 GAAP net income (Q2 had a $37.7m gain of the same kind) and cuts the remaining TRA liability to about $32m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 carried a $37.7m gain of the same kind and the stock fell 1.9%: this line is not paid for.
findings.why_not_priced: Disclosed in an 8-K, so the value (about $0.17 a share, roughly 1.5% of market cap) is public. It may inflate headline GAAP EPS against a $0.36 adjusted consensus and catch an automated headline read for a moment. It has no path to the guide.

findings.finding: The CFO is changing. Pat Thompson stepped down effective 2026-10-01 and leaves 10-30. Tigran Sinanyan (CFO 2015-2021) took over and promises 'disciplined growth'. This is his first quarter setting the Q4 guide.
findings.why_not_priced: The change is public. The inference that a new CFO guides conservatively is not company-confirmed, which is why it is sized small. It came in the same release that firmed up Q3, so the handover does not look forced.
findings.independence: Same document as finding 1 (the 2026-09-03 release). Counts once for the document, but the two lines are different.

findings.finding: Insiders sold steadily under Rule 10b5-1 plans into the print. Director Eugene Nonko sold 332,300 shares between 2026-07-27 and 10-21 in 32 sales, with a further 31,335 noticed on 10-26 (plan adopted 2026-03-03). CRO Keith Cramer sold 12,000 at $11.39 on 10-19 under a plan to cover RSU taxes.
findings.why_not_priced: The sales were pre-scheduled, evenly sized, and paused only in the quiet weeks around the 09-03 update. They carry little information, which is why this is sized near zero.

baseline_tension: The evidence is close to balanced and does not clearly cut against the upside-leaning skew or the +22.6% run-up. The run-up looks like sector beta, the only negative counterparty number (Progressive's slowing policy adds) is a proxy with a profitability offset, and the reported quarter was pre-released, so the Q4 guide decides it and nothing found here settles that guide.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1/6: the Q3 beat sits inside what the company already flagged and this name sold its Q2 beat; finding 1 cut from +0.5 to +0.3.
Lesson 7: a negative run-up/positioning finding goes against an upside-paid skew; cut from -0.5 to -0.3, kept because the chain is too wide (96% spread) to be a strong statement.
Lesson 2: TRA buyout gain is a one-off below operating income with no path to the guide and already disclosed; cut from +0.3 to +0.1.
Lesson 5: LexisNexis shopping series is a proxy for Q3 that the company's own 09-03 update supersedes; cut from -0.3 to -0.2.
Peer demand (EverQuote/QuinStreet) is August information, before MAX's own update; cut from +0.4 to +0.3.
Lesson 3/9: the Progressive finding was already netted against its 88.7 combined ratio and the rest of the customer base; left at -0.5.
CFO-change inference left at -0.2 (rounded from -0.25); insider 10b5-1 sales left at -0.1.

Lesson 8 and the core: abs_move raised from 11 to 12 because hunters understate moves (name median 14.2), trimmed only because Q3 is pre-released; p_up moved from 48 to 49, since the negative lean comes from proxies against the skew and leaning negative into a print is a known bias.
